The [AI Compute Finder](https://uw-compute-finder.vercel.app/) helps UW-Madison researchers choose where to run ML/AI work. Filter by how you want to work, the kind of work, your affiliation, your data and how you pay, then click a platform for its GPUs, limits, cost, data policies and the largest models it can train, fine-tune or serve. Maintained by [DoIT Research Cyberinfrastructure](https://it.wisc.edu/about/division-of-information-technology/research-cyberinfrastructure/); corrections through the **Suggest a correction** link on the site.

## Related resources

- [**Compute**: Center for High Throughput Computing (CHTC)](https://uw-madison-datascience.github.io/ML-X-Nexus/Toolbox/Compute/CHTC.html): The free campus GPU pool.
- [**Compute**: BadgerCompute](https://uw-madison-datascience.github.io/ML-X-Nexus/Toolbox/Compute/BadgerCompute.html): Interactive notebooks with a GPU for short sessions.
- [**Compute**: UW-Madison Cloud Services (AWS, GCP, Azure)](https://uw-madison-datascience.github.io/ML-X-Nexus/Toolbox/Compute/UW-Cloud-Services.html): Institutional cloud accounts and a CHTC-versus-cloud comparison.
- [**Compute**: National Research Platform (NRP)](https://uw-madison-datascience.github.io/ML-X-Nexus/Toolbox/Compute/NRP-Nautilus.html): Free GPUs and hosted open-weight models.
- [**GenAI**: UW Generative AI Services & Policies](https://uw-madison-datascience.github.io/ML-X-Nexus/Toolbox/GenAI/GenAI-at-UW-Madison.html): Which hosted AI services are approved for which data.
